title: Zachary struck silent (Luke 1:5–25)
hookLine: an old priest doubts the angel and can't speak for nine months

cards: Luke's story doesn't open in Bethlehem. It opens in the Temple in Jerusalem, with an old couple. Zachary is a priest, and his wife Elizabeth comes from a priestly family too.

Both, Luke says, were just before God, walking blamelessly. And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were well advanced in years. In that world, that was a grief people could see.
One day, with his division of priests on duty, the lot falls on Zachary to go into the sanctuary and burn incense. He goes in alone.

teach.b: Outside, the crowd is praying at the hour of incense. Inside, Zachary sees an angel standing at the right side of the altar, and he's terrified.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Which prayer? Luke doesn't say.
Some readers hear the old prayer for a child; others, a priest's prayer for his people.
The son will be great, will drink no wine, will be filled with the Holy Ghost, and will go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias.
And Zachary, a good man, standing in the holiest room he'll ever stand in, asks for proof: "Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years."

teach.h: I AM GABRIEL. YOU WILL BE MUTE.
teach.b: The angel answers: I am Gabriel, who stand before God. Because you didn't believe my words, you'll be mute until the day these things happen. Outside, people wonder why he's taking so long.
He comes out and can only make signs, and they realize he's seen a vision. He goes home, and Elizabeth conceives. People often say nine months, but his silence lasts until the baby is born and named.
Is it a punishment? The angel says so. But some readers hear something more.
A priest whose work was prayers and blessings was given a long season with no words, and when his voice comes back, the first thing it does is bless God.
His name, Zachary, means the Lord has remembered.

how: Catholics hear the announcement to Zachary at Mass in the days before Christmas and on the vigil of the Nativity of John the Baptist, and some keep silence before the Blessed Sacrament in Eucharistic adoration.

o: a prophet who anointed the kings of Israel
an old priest whose name means the Lord remembers
the prophet who wrote the Book of Zechariah

games.q: in the Temple — tap the pairs.
p: the name the son must have

s: Zachary's silence lasted exactly nine months
it lasted until the baby was born and named, longer than nine months.
Gabriel told Zachary his prayer was heard
fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard.
it begins in the Temple in Jerusalem, with an old priest burning incense.

games.q: you're Zachary, an old priest alone at the altar of incense. an angel tells you your elderly wife will bear a son. what do you say?
o: thank God, and go out rejoicing.
ask: how shall I know this? I'm an old man.
games.why: "whereby shall I know this?" he asks for proof, and he gets a sign he didn't want: no words until it's fulfilled.

practice: For a couple of minutes, don't talk, even in your head, as much as you can; when words come, let them pass like people walking by a window.
Notice how much of the inner noise is commentary, arguing, planning what to say, and let it quiet down. If you pray, offer the quiet to God and listen.

wordCard.voice: Zachary. The old priest who asked the angel for proof, and could not speak again until his son John was born and named. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Zechariah, the Lord has remembered. in Greek, Zacharias; in the Douay, Zachary.

carryVoice: Your line: silence taught him. When his voice came back, it blessed. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.
